mechanics.name: Quick & Quiet
mechanics.currentEffect: When you perform a Rushed action to vault over a Pallet or Window or to enter or exit a Locker, suppresses all noises related to the interaction and its accompanying Loud Noise Notification. The perk has a 25/20/15-second cooldown.
activation: Perform a Rushed vault over a Pallet or Window, or a Rushed Locker entry or exit.
Ends/deactivates when: The suppression applies to that qualifying interaction; the perk is then unavailable during its cooldown.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.6.0): Reduced cooldown to 25/20/15 seconds and expanded suppression to all interaction noises instead of only reducing the Loud Noise Notification range.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Rushed vaults and Locker entries or exits are silent and do not create their usual Loud Noise Notification, subject to cooldown.
duration: Suppresses noises associated with the qualifying interaction and its accompanying Loud Noise Notification.

editorial.summary: Every 15 seconds at Tier III, a Rushed vault or Locker entry/exit can be completely silent and suppress its Loud Noise Notification.
useCases: Break line of sight and perform a silent Rushed vault so the Killer loses the expected audio and notification cue.
Enter a Locker quickly without advertising the interaction, enabling Head On or stealth mindgames.
Use repeated 15-second-cycle activations during longer chases to create uncertainty at windows and pallets.
counters: The 15-second cooldown can be tracked and exploited by an attentive Killer.
Visual confirmation or direct tracking can make the missing sound irrelevant.
A silent action only matters if the Survivor actually creates uncertainty about their route.
pros: Patch 8.6.0 improved both cooldown and audio suppression.
Works with windows, pallets, and Locker entries or exits.
Can create genuine chase mindgames without requiring a special item or teammate.
cons: Provides no direct speed or health-state protection.
Value depends heavily on line-of-sight breaks and player creativity.
Less useful against Killers whose power or tracking makes the route obvious anyway.
analysis: Quick & Quiet lands at this position because the modern version is substantially better than the old 'hide the loud-noise bubble' perk. Since 8.6.0, it suppresses the interaction noises themselves and can be available every 15 seconds at Tier III, which makes it a repeatable chase tool rather than a once-in-a-while stealth gimmick.

Its strength comes from information denial. Killers often make chase decisions using sound before they regain visual contact. If a Survivor disappears behind a wall and the expected vault sound never occurs, the Killer must spend time verifying the route. That hesitation can create more distance than a raw percentage bonus would suggest.

The perk also has excellent build synergy. Head On turns silent Locker entries into a direct stun threat, Lithe can pair a silent vault with immediate distance, and Deception can create competing Locker information. Even without a dedicated build, a good looper can use Quick & Quiet to make familiar tiles harder to read.

It ranks below Head On because the payoff is indirect. Quick & Quiet does not force the Killer to lose time; the Survivor must construct a believable mindgame. That makes it stronger in experienced hands and weaker for players who simply vault silently but continue running along the most obvious path.
editorial.verdict: A deceptively strong information-denial perk after its modern buffs. Quick & Quiet rewards players who understand how Killers use sound and can turn one missing cue into a real pathing mistake.
